title: Combined Burst Mode versus Torsional Mode Phacoemulsification for Patients with Hard Nuclear Cataracts: A Prospective Comparative Cohort Study

indication: Age-related cataract with Emery-Little nuclear grade III-V (white cataract, previous eye surgery, corneal pathology, uveitis, Fuchs dystrophy and glaucoma excluded; preoperative ECD above 1200 cells/mm2); subgroups by nuclear grade III (moderate) and IV-V (severe)

groups.description: Group A: phacoemulsification in combined burst mode (burst torsional + burst longitudinal ultrasound, Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision, Viscoat; nuclear grade III subgroup (40 eyes, Table 2)

Group A: phacoemulsification in combined burst mode (burst torsional + burst longitudinal ultrasound, Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision, Viscoat; nuclear grade IV-V subgroup (41 + 19 eyes, Table 2)
Group B: phacoemulsification in continuous (linear) torsional mode (Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision, Viscoat; nuclear grade III subgroup (46 eyes, Table 2)
Group B: phacoemulsification in continuous (linear) torsional mode (Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision, Viscoat; nuclear grade IV-V subgroup (41 + 20 eyes, Table 2)

notes: Both phacoemulsification modes are routine settings of the same commercial platform, chosen by the surgeon's routine practice without randomization or an investigational agent: all groups are control-role (same decision as the endothelium record ecd-pmc12994532); nuclear-grade subgroups (predefined baseline condition) are separate control groups. The article frames the combined burst mode as the mode under evaluation against the widely used torsional mode.
Values are mean changes from the subgroup's own pre-operation CCT (value_kind cct_change with reference_cell); Table 4 gives no absolute postoperative CCT.
CCT and ACD measured by Scheimpflug imaging (Oculus Optikgerate GmbH); ECD by an EM-3000 specular microscope (Methods). A single ophthalmologist took the measurements.
